items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: Howard brought in Roy Porter... Roy Porter played the drums and I played the tenor.

ctx.x: Right, my favorite! And we had a great engagement in the Downbeat Club there. And it wasn't too long after that... Well, I'm already in the union and everything now, and I had made a good rapport with Mister Paul Howard, who was the secretary at the Union, and Elmer Fain, he was a delegate, and... I had some fine people. Miss Florence Cadrez; she was assistant to Mister Paul Howard. And right next door to the union (I'd like to get this in) was Lee Young... The Young family lived next door to the union there on…

But anyway, back to Howard McGhee's thing, we had it going pretty good. And Monk was kind of an elder fellow. He was a nice drummer, but he just wasn't into this thing that we were doing. It was a little fast for him, you know. So while we were at the Downbeat, Howard brought in Roy Porter, and he could play the tempos very good.

items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: So I had the experience of working with these guys with Doc's band.

ctx.x: or somebody else would play, and he's got it, just like a continuum, you know.

And there was another trumpet player, ...[INAUDIBLE NAME]... It was the first time I saw a guy playing without the buttons on. He had taken the buttons off the keys, you know. And they called him the Viper. And he was some trumpet player, a very spectacular trumpet player.
